gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-familjen-grotesk: Distinctive from the first glyph, Bruno Ace draws every line like it was ruled out, while Familjen Grotesk lets its bowls stay a little unfinished. Lively against rigid.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-hind: Bruno Ace draws one ruler-straight line from start to finish. Its lingering, one-character-per-beat rhythm earns its place big and brief, while Hind, a sans-serif with lowercase nearly matching its capitals, simply carries on beneath.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-nunito: Nunito reads friendly and contemporary, with big round bowls and terminals that stop well short of the stem. Bruno Ace is best at rod-stock horizontals and verticals, while Nunito is best at soft, generous lowercase.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its tall lowercase tight, with big counters and curves that refuse to close, under Bruno Ace's ruler-drawn heading. Moderate against high lowercase is the real hook.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-quicksand: Blown-glass bulbs under a ruled line. Quicksand's tall lowercase bowls hang beneath Bruno Ace's lingering, constant-width capitals, and the height difference between them keeps the eye moving.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-akatab: Expressive is Bruno Ace's whole attitude, with its ruler-drawn, monoline stroke and counters that stay connected to the outside. Akatab's cupped, rounded letters would read gently going on.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-alan-sans: Wire-smooth and unmistakably drawn: Bruno Ace glides under the eye, one character per beat, with counters left open. Alan Sans sits beneath, a sans-serif whose curve tails stay held back.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-albert-sans: Professional in tone but not timid, Albert Sans keeps its apertures open even at tiny sizes. And Bruno Ace is the display voice, its constant-width line giving the two a clear division of labor.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-alef: Ruled lines, zero stress in any curve: that is Bruno Ace, lingering one character per beat. Alef, a plain sans with open-ended curves throughout, would carry a long passage cleanly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Contemporary and sharply drawn, Bruno Ace holds a stroke with no swell and no thin. Bruno Ace is best at that ruled, lingering display voice, while Alegreya Sans SC, a plain sans, offers a welcoming gap in the c.
